message.reasoning_content: Key risk: step() returns weights.view(N) — a view aliasing the in-place state. Retained history tensors alias the weights storage, so all six "history" entries will show the final w[6] value at observation time. Contract says aliasing itself isn't a failure but the values at observation time must match w[t+1] — so H would be w[6] repeated, which likely fails. Probe passed with 0.0 error... but probe used the same aliasing? Actually probe compared actual_history (also aliased views) with reference — hmm, initial_probe shows error 0.0, odd. Note probe's reference also uses view... no, reference_weights is a clone. Actually initial_probe in kernel.py as source shows error 0.0 recorded on T4 — that's evidence but "not oracle". Interesting: the probe source as written would give history error since actual history aliased. But recorded results say 0.0. That's a discrepancy worth flagging as open question. Also G must be unchanged — kernel doesn't write Gradient, fine. Record update.
